body:
`searchBook` documents that past a couple of hundred hits it "stops and says it stopped". The cap
is applied only AFTER `section.search(query)` has returned its complete array
(frontend/src/lib/reader/searchBook.ts).

The installed epub.js `search()` traverses every text node in the section and pushes every match
before returning; its `maxSeqEle` parameter controls adjacent-node phrase matching, not the result
count. So a single huge chapter with thousands of matches is fully scanned and fully allocated
before all but 200 are discarded.

The cap therefore bounds the returned list and the number of LATER sections, not the cost of the
current one -- the section that most needs bounding. Compounded by the scan being synchronous:
the main thread cannot process the user's own abort while it runs.

Bounding it requires changing the core's contract (a per-section limit passed into the search, or
chunked traversal), which is why it was not folded into the UI PR.

Found by adversarial review (Terra).
title: The search hit cap does not bound work inside a single section
